basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 9-11.' and it opens 'Vers. 9, 11. Deus patris mei Abraham, erue me de manu fratris mei. Dum ergo et sibi'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 9, 11. Deus patris mei Abraham, erue me de manu fratris mei. Dum ergo et sibi providet, et Deum orat, dat nobis exemplum ut vitae nostrae provideamus, et tamen divinum auxilium nobis adesse rogemus.
